transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, honestly, I'm just... I'm here because my body feels completely out of my control, and it's been terrifying, to be frank. It started a little while ago, I don't even know exactly when, but I was just so wired. I couldn't stop moving. I was pacing around my apartment, literally all night long, just walking back and forth, back and forth, from the kitchen to the living room, making all these incredibly detailed notes for this supper-club concept I was going to start. I had menus, seating charts, lighting ideas, everything. I just couldn't sit still, my legs just had to keep going. But then... then it just completely flipped. Lately, I'm just so incredibly slowed down. It's like moving through molasses. My sister, she came over the other day, and she actually got mad at me because she said it took me forever just to put my shoes on. Like, just tying the laces felt like this monumental task that required all my energy. It's just so bizarre, going from not being able to stop moving to barely being able to lift my foot, you know? It's really messing with my shifts at the restaurant, too, because you can't be slow when you're waiting tables, but I just can't make my body do what I want it to do anymore.
Have you experienced periods where you felt extremely sad or hopeless?

Sad? Hopeless? No, I... I wouldn't say that. It's really not like that at all. I mean, I'm not sitting around crying or feeling sorry for myself, you know? It's not like this dark cloud of misery or anything. It's more just... well, it's exactly what I was saying about my body. 

Like, my mom called me the other day, and she was asking if I was depressed because I haven't been going out with my friends from college—some of the guys I used to take classes with before I took a break to work full-time—and I had to spend like twenty minutes explaining to her, like, Mom, I'm not sad. I don't feel like the world is ending. I just literally cannot summon the physical energy to walk down the three flights of stairs in my apartment building and get on the subway. 

It's just so incredibly frustrating because everyone assumes that if you're moving slow and not doing much, you must be heartbroken or miserable or something. But honestly, I don't feel hopeless about my life or my future. I just... I just feel completely trapped in my own muscles right now. Does that make sense? Like, the sadness isn't there, just this overwhelming physical drag that I absolutely cannot shake, no matter how much espresso I try to chug in the breakroom before my shifts. So, yeah, no, not sad. Just stuck.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or on top of the world?

Happy? Well, happy isn't quite the right word. It was more like... well, okay, so this was a few months ago, right around the time I got fired from this other restaurant I was working at. It was this upscale Italian place downtown, and honestly, the management was terrible, totally incompetent. So when they let me go, you'd think I'd be upset, right? Most people would be freaking out about rent or whatever. But I didn't care at all. I actually felt... I felt completely unstoppable. Like, weirdly excited and just buzzing with this intense energy, like getting fired was the best thing that could have possibly happened to me because it freed me up for my real purpose. 

I felt like I was on top of the world, like you said, but it was almost too much. I was walking around the city feeling like I knew the secrets to the universe, like I was going to revolutionize the entire hospitality industry. I was so amped up. But the thing is, it wasn't all sunshine and rainbows. Because I felt so brilliant and capable, I had zero patience for anyone else. If someone didn't get my vision, or if they tried to tell me to slow down or be realistic—like my roommate, he kept telling me I needed to apply for unemployment and I just went off on him. I mean, I would just completely blow up. I'd scream at people, like they were actively trying to sabotage me or ruin my life just by asking a simple question. It was this intense high, but with this really sharp, angry edge to it if anyone got in my way. So, yeah, I felt incredible, but God help you if you didn't agree with me.
How long did this unstoppable, energetic feeling last after you got fired?

Well, let me think... so I got let go from that Italian place right around the beginning of the fall, I think it was late September or maybe early October? Yeah, definitely around then because I remember the leaves were just starting to change when I was walking around the city feeling so completely electric. And honestly, that feeling... that whole unstoppable, buzzing, top-of-the-world thing where I was sketching out all those supper-club ideas and just pacing all night? It didn't just go away in a few days. It really stuck around. 

Actually, if I really track it back, it's been going on for about four months now. Like, four whole months of this completely wild ride starting right after I got fired. I mean, it wasn't exactly the exact same intensity every single second of those four months, obviously, because eventually I crashed into this awful slowness I was telling you about, but that whole period of time, that whole four-month block starting from the firing, has just been this completely abnormal state for me. It's like a switch got flipped the day they handed me my final paycheck, and for four months, my brain and my body have just been doing whatever they want, completely hijacking my life. Like, four months is a long time to feel like you're not driving your own car, you know? And it's just so frustrating trying to explain that timeline to people who think I'm just having a couple of weird days.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't hear or see during these periods of extreme energy or slowness?

Voices? Like hallucinations? No, no, I haven't had anything like that. I mean, I know that can happen to some people when they get really stressed out or, you know, when their brain is going a million miles an hour, but for me, it was never like that. I never saw things that weren't there or heard people talking to me when I was alone in my apartment. 

I mean, don't get me wrong, my thoughts were incredibly loud during those four months, especially when I was feeling so unstoppable and electric. It felt like I had a hundred different ideas shouting at me all at once, all these brilliant plans for the hospitality industry, but they were my thoughts, you know? It wasn't like a voice coming from outside my head or from the corner of the room. It was just my own brain running on overdrive, so fast and so intense that it was almost deafening, but still definitely me. 

And even now, with this horrible physical heaviness and feeling like I can't even drag myself down the stairs, it's just quiet. Too quiet, almost. But there are no voices telling me things or shadows moving in the corners or anything spooky like that. I've always been really grounded in reality that way, even when my reality feels completely hijacked by my own energy levels. Like, I might have been screaming at my roommate because I thought he was dragging me down, but I knew it was my roommate, and I knew what I was saying. I wasn't, like, talking to ghosts or anything. So, no, definitely no voices or visions or anything like that. Just the extreme highs and this terrible, stuck feeling I have right now.
Do these periods of feeling unstoppable and then really slowed down happen one after the other, or can you have both feelings at the same time?

Both at the same time? Wow, okay, let me think about that. I mean, usually, it feels like they're pretty separate, you know? Like, when I was in that zone after getting fired, when I was pacing the apartment and sketching out all those business plans and screaming at my roommate, that was just pure, unadulterated energy. I was moving a hundred miles an hour, and there was no slowness there at all. It was just go, go, go. And then, when I crashed, it was like hitting a brick wall. The energy just completely evaporated, and I was left with this... this awful, heavy feeling where I couldn't even get out of bed to make coffee. 

So, it's mostly been one extreme or the other, like a pendulum swinging from way up high to way down low. I don't really remember a specific time where I felt like I was bursting with that unstoppable energy but also feeling physically heavy and slowed down at the exact same moment. I mean, I guess there might be like a transition day, maybe? Like a day where the energy is starting to drain out of me and the heaviness is creeping in, but even then, it's not like I'm experiencing both full-blown states simultaneously. It's more like one is taking over while the other is fading away. 

But, you know, my memory of those transition periods is a little blurry because it's just so chaotic when my brain is shifting gears like that. But yeah, generally speaking, it's been a pretty clear sequence: first the extreme high, the buzzing, the grand ideas, and then... boom. The crash. The slowness. The feeling like I'm moving through molasses. It's exhausting just thinking about how drastically different those two states are, and to imagine them happening at the exact same time? Man, I think my brain would just short-circuit completely. So, no, I haven't really noticed them happening simultaneously. It's pretty much one, and then eventually, the other.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns during these periods of feeling unstoppable or really slowed down?

Sleep? Oh man, sleep has been a total disaster, just completely all over the map. When I was in that whole electric, top-of-the-world phase right after I got let go from the restaurant, sleep was basically non-existent. Like, I genuinely didn't need it. I remember there was this one stretch, maybe a Tuesday through a Thursday, where I think I maybe laid down for twenty minutes on the couch, but my brain was just vibrating so hard I had to get back up. I was pacing the living room, sketching out floor plans for this supper club idea I had, looking up commercial real estate listings at three in the morning, and I felt completely fine. Better than fine, actually. I felt like I had tapped into some secret reserve of energy that normal people don't have. My roommate would wake up at 7 AM for work, and I'd already have brewed a pot of coffee and reorganized the entire kitchen pantry, and I wouldn't even feel tired. It was like sleep was just this massive waste of time when I could be doing so many brilliant things. I think I went weeks on maybe two or three hours a night, tops, and I felt invincible.

But then... yeah, then the crash happened. And when the slowness hit, the sleep thing completely flipped. It’s like my body suddenly realized it hadn’t rested in a month and just shut down entirely. Now, with this heavy, dragging feeling? All I want to do is sleep. I’ll sleep for twelve, thirteen, fourteen hours, and I still wake up feeling like I haven't slept at all. Like, I'll go to bed at 9 PM, sleep all the way through the night, wake up at noon the next day, and getting out from under the covers feels like trying to lift a boulder off my chest. I'll drag myself to the bathroom, maybe drink a glass of water, and then I'm just exhausted all over again and have to go back to bed. It’s so frustrating because I know I’m sleeping so much, way more than a normal person should, but it doesn't do anything. It doesn't refresh me or give me any energy back. It’s just this endless, heavy hibernation. So yeah, the sleep changes have been drastic. From not needing it at all and feeling like Superman, to sleeping half the day away and still feeling completely dead to the world. It’s just exhausting trying to keep up with what my body wants.
Do you think these periods of feeling unstoppable and then really slowed down might be connected to your menstrual cycle in any way?

Wait, my menstrual cycle? Uh... I'm a guy, so, no, I definitely don't have one of those. I mean, I guess I understand why you might ask if you're just going down a standard medical checklist or something, because I know hormones can completely mess with people's moods. My older sister used to get really intense around her time of the month, but yeah, for me, being a twenty-five-year-old guy, that's definitely not the culprit. 

Though, honestly, I have spent so much time trying to figure out if there is some kind of cycle or pattern to all of this. Like, I've analyzed literally everything else in my life to death. I thought maybe it was the weather, or the seasons changing, or even my diet. When I was working at the restaurant before they let me go, I was eating a lot of terrible food, just grabbing fries off the line during the dinner rush, working these insane double shifts where you're just constantly on your feet, carrying heavy trays, dealing with angry customers and the kitchen staff yelling... I thought maybe the sheer stress of that environment just finally snapped something in my brain and triggered that massive wave of energy. 

But even then, it doesn't really follow a predictable schedule like a biological cycle would, you know? It just kind of happened. One day I was just a regular waiter, and the next I was vibrating with a thousand business ideas. And now I'm just stuck in this heavy, awful phase, trying to trace it all back to some root cause. I've literally laid in bed for hours these past few weeks, just staring at the ceiling, trying to connect the dots and find out what set it all off. It drives me crazy not knowing why my brain is doing this. But yeah, to answer your question, it's definitely not a menstrual cycle. That's about the only thing I can rule out with one hundred percent certainty right now.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely confident or invincible, and engaged in risky behaviors without thinking through the consequences?

Oh, absolutely. Invincible doesn't even begin to cover it. It was like... like I had cracked some cosmic code that everyone else was too blind to see. I mentioned that supper club idea earlier, right? Well, let me just give you an idea of where my head was at with that. 

I honestly, truly believed, deep down in my bones, that I was about to build the absolute best bilingual supper club in the entire city. I mean, I had the whole thing mapped out in my head and on these massive pieces of poster board all over the apartment. I was designing the menus—this incredible fusion concept—picking out the velvet upholstery for the booths, planning the live music schedules, everything. I was so utterly convinced it was a goldmine that I figured investors would be stupid not to back me. Like, I genuinely thought they would be begging to throw their money at me once they saw my vision. 

And the crazy part, the really risky part where I just wasn't thinking about consequences at all, was that I was doing all of this right after getting fired. I didn't have a job. I had zero income coming in. I had absolutely no money lined up, my savings were basically a joke, but it just didn't matter to me. It didn't even register as a problem. I was putting massive charges on my credit cards, buying up all these premium website domain names, paying some graphic designer I found online at three in the morning to make these elaborate logos, printing out these glossy, expensive pitch decks... 

My roommate was freaking out, trying to talk to me about how we were going to pay rent, and I just laughed at him. I literally laughed in his face because I was so sure I was about to be a millionaire. I told him he was thinking too small, that he was stuck in the rat race while I was building an empire. I felt like I had the Midas touch, you know? Like every single thought in my head was just pure, unadulterated genius, and the regular rules of life—like needing a job, or having actual capital before starting a restaurant—they just didn't apply to me anymore. Looking back on it now from where I am, just feeling so heavy and awful and looking at my credit card statements, it’s completely humiliating. But in that moment? Man, I felt like a god. I really thought I was untouchable.
How have these episodes of feeling unstoppable and then really slowed down affected your relationships with friends and family?

It's... honestly, it's just completely wrecked everything. Like, I don't even know where things stand with anyone anymore. I mean, I mentioned my roommate earlier, right? The whole rent arrangement completely fell apart. Because, you know, I haven't been able to hold together any actual work plans. I was so focused on that supper club fantasy, just absolutely convinced I was on the verge of greatness, that I completely ignored the reality that I didn't have a job and needed to pay for my half of the apartment. So now he's furious, and I really don't blame him, because I left him completely high and dry while I was blowing money on nothing. 

But it's not just him, it's... it's my family, too. I've completely dropped the ball on all my family commitments. Like, I missed my mom's birthday dinner a while back because I was in that weird, vibrating, untouchable phase and I honestly thought I was too busy and too important, just "networking" online and drawing up those floor plans. And then, when the crash hit... man, I couldn't even text anyone back to apologize. I couldn't get basic responsibilities organized on my own. I'm talking about things like opening a piece of mail, or taking out the trash, or even just calling my mom to tell her I was alive—it all just felt impossible. 

I was just a ghost in my own life. It got so bad, just me lying there in the dark for days, that my older sister—the one I mentioned before—she actually had to come over and physically intervene. She had been trying to call me, and when I didn't answer, she just let herself in. She took one look at the state of my room, and the state of me, and she just... she had to pack me into her car and take me to the crisis clinic. Because I was just so completely incapable of functioning. I couldn't organize a single basic thing to keep myself going. It’s just so embarrassing, you know? Having your older sister have to lead you by the hand to a clinic because you can't even manage to put on your own shoes or figure out how to exist. So, yeah, my relationships are pretty much hanging by a thread right now. It's just a mess.
Have you had more than one of these cycles of feeling unstoppable and then really slowed down?

Honestly, I really don't know. I mean, I'm not sure. I've actually been trying to map out my entire life in my head while lying in the dark these past few weeks, just running through every single memory I have, trying to figure out if there's a pattern I missed. 

Like, I look back and think, was there another time? I've definitely had periods where I was really into a project, or times when I felt pretty down. Like, when I first left college, I was pretty bummed out. I just slept on my buddy's couch for, I don't know, a month or something? Just eating junk food, watching awful daytime TV, and completely ignoring my phone. But at the time, I just thought, well, I'm a twenty-year-old guy who doesn't know what to do with his life, of course I'm going to be in a funk. Was that a crash? I have no idea. 

And then there were times I felt super energized. Like when I first started at that restaurant, before things went bad, I was picking up every single shift they would give me. I was working like sixty hours a week, and then going out with the bartenders and the kitchen staff afterward until three or four in the morning, and waking up at nine to do it all over again. But everybody in the service industry does that, you know? It’s just the culture. You run on caffeine and adrenaline. 

So, I try to compare those older times to what just happened with the whole supper club thing and this... this absolute black hole I'm in right now. And it's like comparing apples and, I don't know, chainsaws. What I just went through, this massive peak where I thought I was a literal genius who didn't need sleep or money, followed by this total inability to even take out the trash or answer my sister's calls... I really don't think I've ever had a full, extreme cycle like *this* before. Or maybe I have, and it was just a smaller version of it, and I just didn't recognize it for what it was? 

I honestly couldn't tell you for sure. My brain is just so foggy and heavy right now, I feel like I can't even trust my own memories. I just keep playing my whole life on a loop trying to find the thread, but yeah, I really don't know if this exact kind of up-and-down thing has happened more than once.
Did you ever feel like you were so energetic and confident that you didn't need to sleep for several days in a row?

I mean... several days in a row? Like, zero sleep at all for, what, 48 or 72 hours straight? I... I don't think it was exactly like that. I mean, I know I just said a minute ago that I felt like I didn't need sleep, and that was completely true at the time—like, in my head, sleep was just this massive, pointless waste of time that was keeping me from building my empire. I had too much to do. But if I really try to sit here and piece the actual timeline together... which is incredibly hard right now because my brain just feels like it's full of wet cement... I don't think I went completely without closing my eyes for days on end. 

I was definitely up at all hours, though. Like I said, I was emailing that graphic designer at three in the morning, and I'd be pacing holes into the living room rug, moving my poster boards around, and then the sun would come up and I wouldn't even feel a drop of exhaustion. I'd just brew a whole pot of coffee and keep right on going. But I think... I must have been taking these really intense, bizarre little micro-naps. Like, I'd maybe crash face-first onto the couch for an hour or two in the middle of the afternoon, just completely pass out on top of my menu sketches, and then I'd jolt right back awake, heart pounding, totally wired and ready to tackle the world again. 

So I was running on practically nothing, just fumes and pure adrenaline, and my roommate was definitely looking at me like I was a crazy person because I was always awake when he went to bed and awake when he got up. But... yeah, as far as being completely awake for several full days in a row without a single second of sleep? I haven't really noticed that being the case. Or, at least, I can't be sure. The whole week or two just blends together into this one long, continuous, crazy day of velvet upholstery and pitch decks, you know? I just remember the energy, not the clock.
Have you experienced more than one episode of feeling unstoppable followed by a crash into extreme slowness in your life?

I think we... wait, didn't we just talk about this a second ago? Or maybe I misunderstood what you meant the first time, but yeah, like I was saying before, I really don't know. I honestly can't give you a solid yes or no. I've been sitting here, well, not just here but for the past couple of weeks, just completely trapped in my own head trying to figure that exact thing out. 

I keep trying to put my past into these neat little boxes, you know? Like, trying to dissect every single mood I've had since I was a teenager. Was that time I dropped my classes and just lay around my buddy's apartment a crash? Was that time I worked all those double shifts at the restaurant and felt like I was on top of the world a peak? I keep trying to draw a line connecting all these dots, but the more I try to force my memories to fit into this exact pattern of being totally unstoppable and then completely paralyzed, the more confused I get. 

Because nothing in my past feels quite as extreme as what just happened with the supper club and then ending up at the crisis clinic. It's like, sure, I've had good weeks and bad weeks, everyone has those, but a full-on, massive cycle like this? I just haven't noticed it happening before. Or if it did, I was completely blind to it at the time and just wrote it off as normal life stuff. I'm sorry, I know you're trying to get a clear timeline here and I'm probably not making your job very easy, but my head is just swimming right now. I keep going around and around in circles trying to answer that for you, and I just... I really don't have a better answer than what I said a minute ago. I just don't know if it's happened more than once.
Have you experienced more than one episode of these extreme mood swings in your life?

Doc, I... I feel like I'm losing my mind a little bit here, because I swear we literally just went over this, right? Like, twice now? 

I really, really want to give you the exact answer you're looking for, I do. I know you're trying to fill out a chart or figure out a timeline, but I just don't have it. I mean, "extreme mood swings"... what even counts as extreme? Because compared to this whole supper club disaster, everything else in my entire life just feels like a tiny ripple in a pond. I've been racking my brain—which, again, feels like it's stuffed with wet cotton right now—trying to map out every single time I felt really good or really bad. 

And sure, like I said, there were times I was super hyped up about picking up double shifts, or times I couldn't get off my friend's couch for a month. But were they *extreme*? Were they like *this*? I just don't know. It's so frustrating because I feel like I should know my own life story, you know? I should be able to look back and say, "Oh yeah, back when I was 22, I had a massive mood swing." But it's all just a blur of restaurant jobs, late nights, cheap coffee, and me just trying to figure things out. 

So if you're asking if I've had more than one of these exact, massive, completely unhinged swings where I think I'm a god and then suddenly I can't even speak... I honestly haven't noticed it happening before. Or at least, I'm just not sure. I'm sorry, I know I'm rambling and not giving you a straight yes or no, but I really just don't know.
Have you experienced episodes of feeling unstoppable followed by a crash into extreme slowness more than once in your life?

Okay, I... I really don't mean to be difficult, I promise I don't. But I feel like we are just going in circles now. Are you... is there a specific reason you keep asking me this same exact thing? Because I really, truly do not know what else to tell you. I feel like I'm failing a test here. 

I mean, "unstoppable followed by a crash." Yes, that is exactly what just happened. The supper club, the velvet chairs, the pitch decks, the feeling like I could see the matrix of the entire restaurant industry... and then waking up feeling like I was buried under a ton of bricks and ending up at the clinic. Yes, that happened. That was the last few weeks. 

But *more than once*? I... I just can't say. I've been sitting here trying so hard to rewind the tape of my life for you. I'm trying to look at when I was 19 and dropped out of those college classes. Was I slow then? Was I crashed? Or was I just a lazy 19-year-old who hated macroeconomics? And what about when I was 21 and worked all those doubles at the steakhouse and felt like I was the best waiter on the planet? Was I unstoppable, or was I just making really good tips and drinking too much espresso? 

I can't tell the difference! It's like you're asking me to look at a giant, messy painting of my life and point out all the blue spots, but I'm colorblind and everything just looks gray. I don't know if this massive, terrifying roller coaster ride has happened before, because nothing else in my life has ever felt this big or this destructive. So... I just don't know. I really, really don't know.
Have you experienced episodes of feeling unstoppable followed by a crash into extreme slowness before this recent incident?

Doctor... I really, I mean this with all due respect, but are you trying to trick me? Or is this some kind of memory test? Because I feel like I'm losing my mind here, and I'm already pretty sure I've lost my mind, given that I'm sitting in a psychiatrist's office after trying to start a million-dollar supper club with zero dollars. 

I just... I don't know how many different ways I can say it. Before this recent incident? Before the velvet chairs and the endless talking and then the complete, suffocating darkness? I don't know. I honestly, genuinely, 100 percent do not know. 

I keep trying to explain it. I keep trying to give you the context of my life so you can see why this is so hard for me to answer. You're asking me to look back at my entire life—twenty-five years of just... living, you know? And you want me to pick out these specific moments of being "unstoppable" or "crashing." But my life before this just felt like a normal life. Sure, maybe a little chaotic. I'm a waiter, you know? The restaurant industry is chaotic. You work a Friday night rush, you're slammed, you're energized, you feel like you're flying. Is that being unstoppable? And then you wake up the next day at 2 PM and you can't drag yourself out of bed because you're so exhausted. Is that a crash? 

I just can't separate normal life from whatever this is that you're looking for. I mean, I dropped out of college. I spent weeks just lying around doing nothing. Was that a crash? Or was I just depressed because I didn't know what I wanted to do with my life? I can't look back and confidently say, "Yes, Doctor, I had an episode." Because nothing, absolutely nothing, has ever felt as extreme, as terrifying, as out of control as what just happened to me over the last month. So if you're asking if I've had *this* before... I really don't think so. But if you're asking if I've ever felt really good and then really bad? Yeah, of course. Everyone has. I just... I don't have the answer you want. I'm sorry. I really am.
Have you experienced any other episodes similar to this recent one, where you felt unstoppable and then crashed into extreme slowness, at any other point in your life?

Doctor... are you... I mean, are you even listening to me? Or are you just reading off a list of questions on a clipboard and ticking boxes? Because I feel like I am screaming into a void here. I... I really don't know how to make this any clearer. 

Look, I get it. I get that you need to know if this is a pattern. You want to know if my brain has been doing this my whole life and I just didn't notice, or if this supper club thing was some weird, one-off explosion. But I am telling you, I do not know. I have literally zero idea. 

When you ask if I've had "other episodes similar to this recent one"... what does "similar" mean? Does it mean I felt a little energetic? Because yeah, like I said, working a double shift on a Saturday night when the kitchen is in the weeds and I'm juggling six tables and somehow keeping it all together—that feels pretty unstoppable. You feel like a superhero. And then Sunday morning, you can barely move your legs and your brain feels like mush. Is that what you mean? Because if so, then yes, it's happened a hundred times! 

But if you mean... if you mean feeling like I actually, truly believed I was going to revolutionize the culinary world, like I was vibrating at a frequency nobody else could see, and then crashing so hard that I couldn't even speak to the intake nurse here... no. No, I don't think so. I mean, nothing has ever been this intense. Nothing has ever blown up my life like this. 

Before this, I was just a guy trying to figure out if I should go back to school or try to get promoted to head server. I wasn't... I wasn't *this*. I wasn't a guy who needed to be in a psychiatrist's office. So, please, I am begging you, can we just agree that I don't know? Can we please just move on from this question? Because my head is pounding, I feel like I'm trapped in a loop, and I really, really don't have a different answer for you. I just don't.
Have you experienced any episodes similar to this recent one before it happened?

I... I actually don't know what is happening right now. Are you... is this some kind of psychiatric technique? Like, if you ask me the exact same question five times in a row, I'm suddenly going to unlock a secret hidden memory? Because I promise you, there is no secret memory. There is just me, sitting here, feeling like my blood has been replaced with wet cement, begging you to hear the words coming out of my mouth.

I don't know what magic word you are waiting for me to say. I really don't. I have gone through my college years for you. I have gone through my weekend shifts at the steakhouse. I've told you about the normal chaos of just being a twenty-five-year-old guy trying to pay rent and figure things out. I've laid out my entire adult life in this room, trying to give you whatever clue you're digging for, and I keep telling you that none of it—literally zero percent of it—felt like the absolute hurricane of this last month. 

Before the supper club thing happened, before I was sketching out velvet seating arrangements on napkins at 4 AM and feeling like I was a god of hospitality, and then crashing into this... this absolute nothingness I'm in right now... no.
